Article Title: China, Russia’s reality check for Trump: Why US sanctions may not matter any more
Article Text:
What has changed? Why is the world less affected by US sanctions?

Also check:

How the US built its sanctions power

Diminshing impact of US sanctions power

Fossil Fuel Shipment Departures From Russia

How Northern Sea Route Works For China

Countries with Most Rare Earths

What this means for US

Outstanding foreign official Treasury Holdings

Reaction of 10-year Treasury yield to sanctions

What it means for India

Trump waives Russia-related sanctions for India

For a long time, secondary sanctions have served to be an effective tool for the US. The Donald Trump administration has been aggressively using them in a bid to exercise geoeconomic influence over individuals, businesses and banks linked to countries that it considers as adversaries.In fact, for many years, these measures have proved to be highly effective tools of economic pressure. From the 1980s to the 2010s, the US increasingly used secondary sanctions to transform the dollar-based financial system into a powerful instrument for exerting geopolitical pressure and isolating foreign governments and companies.But that seems to be changing now. Tariffs, secondary sanctions and more - the Donald Trump administration has all tried several tricks up its sleeve to browbeat the global economy. But, the world has survived.A recent report by Henrich Foundation notes: “Overwhelming US sanctions power was for many years a strategic substitute for US military power projection, allowing the economic containment of rival states and thereby freeing up military resources for prime theaters such as the Middle East and East Asia.“In both these regions, however, US military power and sanctions power now appear less capable of deterrence than before,” it says.What has changed? Why is the world less affected by US sanctions and what does this mean for India?For decades, the United States relied on its overwhelming ability to impose sanctions as an alternative to projecting military power. Economic restrictions helped Washington contain rival states while allowing it to reserve military resources for strategically important regions, particularly the Middle East and East Asia.Whether it was the 2000s or 2010s, the US used secondary sanctions to compel European banks to comply with restrictions that were targeted at Iran, Sudan and Cuba.It all started with the growing strength of the dollar as part of the integrated global trading system from the 1980s onwards. This raised the economic cost for countries of being cut off from the US dollar system.According to the Henrich Foundation report, “The traded goods share of global GDP rose continuously from 36% of global GDP in 1979 to 55% of global GDP in 2015.”By the late 1990s and the 2000s, the dollar had firmly established itself not just as the world's leading reserve currency, but also an important invoicing currency, borrowing currency, source of liquidity and vehicle currency for foreign investment.The United States also benefited from a substantial imbalance in economic power. Its position gave it a significant advantage over countries targeted by sanctions, which had relatively few options to retaliate against Washington's economic measures.A further factor underpinning US sanctions’ power was the period of relative macroeconomic stability that lasted from the mid-1980s until the mid-2010s.According to Henrich, from 2010 onward, a fourth pillar further enhanced the US ability to target the main commodity export of its rivals: oil production.“Thanks to easy financing conditions, the US experienced a domestic shale oil boom and became a net exporter of fossil fuels,” its report says.Fundamentally, as the risk of sanctions has become more persistent, countries have grown increasingly interested in protecting themselves against their exposure to the US dollar.The Henrich report notes since 2017, and particularly after the “Liberation Day” tariffs that were introduced in spring 2025, US tariff measures have prompted changes in the configuration of global supply chains.“The growing use of export controls on all kinds of strategic items - semiconductors and chipmaking equipment, AI technology, rare earths, and so on - is driving companies and governments to invest in domestic production capacity and in stronger alliance networks that can secure these technologies,” the report says.“On the whole, the world economy has weathered the impact of trade conflict and economic warfare,” it adds.In fact, the report cautions that recent economic research indicates that these developments may weaken US power more severely and more quickly than measures of its overall control over global networks might imply.One of the biggest examples of the diminishing power of America’s secondary sanctions is the strong shadow tanker fleet that continues to globally transport Russian energy supplies.US sanctions against Iran and Venezuela during the 2010s, followed by the coordinated G7 measures against Russia in the early 2020s, progressively excluded several major oil-producing countries from the unrestricted international market centred on the Brent crude benchmark.However, these restrictions did not eliminate the trade in oil. Instead, they redirected it towards alternative channels that are harder to monitor. The global oil market has, in effect, split into two segments: a largely unrestricted market accounting for most oil traded internationally, and a smaller but still substantial “shadow” market created by sanctions.“To supply the growing shadow market in oil, an entire ecosystem of tankers, shipping companies, and insurers formed. Many of this network’s participants function to facilitate the joint trade of Venezuela, Iran, and Russia, while supplying oil importers such as China, India, Türkiye, Vietnam, Indonesia, and others,” the report says.“Despite voluminous and regular new sanctions designations on these ships, companies, and facilitators, secondary sanctions have not proven capable of meaningfully reducing or permanently denting this gray oil market,” the report adds.Not only that, Russia is actively exploring the Northern Sea Route for its exports.And then come China and Iran.China’s restrictions on rare earth exports, alongside Iran’s capacity to disrupt shipping in the Gulf and interfere with oil and gas production in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, have given these countries economic tools with which to push back directly against the US.“This development was apparent in October 2025, when a Chinese embargo on its rare earth exports forced Donald Trump to accept a tariff truce in the Sino-US trade war. Faced with growing shortages in US manufacturing and the defense industry, Trump agreed at an important meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at Busan in South Korea not to impose new export controls and to revert several recent controls on chip exports to China,’ the report explains.Caught off guard by US sanctions targeting its telecommunications sector and chipmakers in 2018–2019, Beijing has spent considerable effort developing a strategy to retaliate with economic pressure during Donald Trump’s second term. Since then, China has further expanded its permanent export-control machinery, ensuring that it can keep this option available for use whenever necessary.“Any significant new US export controls and tariffs risk reactivating a painful Chinese response. But because this stability rests on a commitment to US abstinence from serious secondary sanctions against Chinese entities, Washington’s freedom of maneuver in this space is reduced in the long run,” the report says.Iran, too, has demonstrated its capacity to affect the US economy in 2026. The impact is less immediate and operates through indirect channels, but restrictions on traffic through the Strait of Hormuz have triggered a global fuel crisis with consequences for the American economy.Despite being a major exporter of fossil fuels, the US remains vulnerable to oil price shocks in particular product markets.Iran’s strategic position in the Strait of Hormuz, combined with Russia’s natural gas exports, gives the two countries control over approximately 42% of the global natural gas market, covering both liquefied natural gas and supplies transported through pipelines.China, Iran and Russia have built up countervailing economic leverage across a range of critical resources, from rare earth metals to natural gas and petroleum products. Although these capabilities do not eliminate the considerable geoeconomic power that the US Treasury retains through secondary sanctions, they have made it harder for Washington to deploy economic coercion without facing resistance.Yet another important point to note is that the effects of US sanctions are increasingly being felt in the Treasury market as foreign governments are reducing their exposure to US debt.The report points out that foreign official holdings fell 8.4% from $4.24 trillion in January 2021 to $3.87 trillion in December 2025, while China has more than halved its holdings over the past decade. This has given Beijing greater scope to use Treasury sales to pressure Washington.The trend accelerated after the US attack on Iran, with overseas public-sector holdings dropping 6.3% between February and August 2026, including a 31% fall in short-term Treasury bills to $312 billion.For India, the news is mixed. Sanctions are seen as an economic leverage, but India has till now not finalised a trade deal with the US, insisting on a competitive advantage. It has also not stopped buying Russian crude. Resilience in exports through diversified markets and trade agreements has also helped in India.According to Vivek Iyer, Partner and Financial Services Risk Advisory Leader, Grant Thornton Bharat, India is moderately exposed to sanctions pressure, and in a few concentrated areas.“The thesis that alternative networks blunt sanctions mostly helps countries that are themselves sanctioned, like Russia and Iran. India is a third country. Its banks, exporters and refiners rely heavily on dollar clearing and US markets, so a secondary-sanctions threat still works on India even if it has weakened against Russia,” he tells TOI.Energy remains the biggest exposure. The new Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act allows the US to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from the five biggest buyers of Russian oil and gas. India, which takes more Russian crude than any country except China, is one of them.On October 16, Trump waived sections 112 and 113 and most of the Act's sanctions provisions, but that waiver is discretionary and can be reversed. Russia's share of India's crude imports was roughly 56% at its height and fell to about 35% in September.And there is a past precedent to US pressure when Trump imposed a 25% penal tariff on India for its Russian oil purchases. India did not stop buying Russian crude oil due to tariffs, but subsequent sanctions on Russian oil majors did force it to recalibrate oil procurement strategy.Yet, the US needs India both strategically and in oil markets.Ajay Srivastava, founder, Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) believes that India remains vulnerable at both the company and country levels.“The risk has already shaped India’s energy choices. India stopped buying Iranian crude and previously cut back on Venezuelan oil to avoid US sanctions. The Russian oil tariff showed how a dispute over energy imports can reach Indian exporters with no connection to the oil trade,” he tells TOI.Yet, to a point tougher US sanctions may benefit India.“For the US, the costs show up as higher oil prices (the Rosneft/Lukoil sanctions precipitated an 8% increase in global Brent crude oil prices), tariffs paid by US consumers, and faster growth of alternative payment systems. For India, the possible gains include discounted crude, more trade settled in rupees, GIFT City attracting flows that are being diverted, and better market access if it lines up with the US,” Vivek Iyer tells TOI.
Article Summary: For decades, the United States relied on its overwhelming ability to impose sanctions as an alternative to projecting military power. Tariffs, secondary sanctions and more - the Donald Trump administration has all tried several tricks up its sleeve to browbeat the global economy. But, the world has survived.

Article Title: Trump’s Nvidia stake grew to as much as $62 million: Report
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

Trump's Nvidia stake

White House response to questions over Trump's Nvidia holdings

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

‘She may not be a spy,’ says Trump

US President Donald Trump has stood by Nvidia’s former boss Jensen Huang despite a string of personal scandals, including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.But there is another Nvidia connection drawing attention: Trump's own stock portfolio.His investments in the AI chipmaker have grown sharply over the past year, with financial disclosures suggesting that his stake could be worth as much as $62 million.The disclosures put Trump's Nvidia holdings under the spotlight as the company grapples with controversy surrounding Huang's resignation and its business dealings with China.Trump’s Nvidia holdings, estimated at between $615,000 and $1.3 million at the end of 2024, rose to as much as $62 million within the last year, according to financial disclosures reviewed by The Washington Post. However, these filings do not include trades made over the past two months, so the latest value of his holdings could be even higher, The Independent reported.But the value of his holdings is only part of the picture. Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have been actively buying and selling Nvidia shares.A CNBC analysis of his annual and periodic financial disclosures found that his accounts had bought or sold Nvidia shares at least 103 times.The transactions were worth a combined $27 million to $97.5 million.The exact size of Trump's current stake, however, remains unclear. His disclosures report investments in broad dollar-value ranges rather than the actual number of shares held. Based on the holdings reported in August, his Nvidia investment would have been worth between $4.5 million and $57.7 million by midday Monday, when the stock was trading at around $157.The latest disclosures do not capture transactions from the past two months, making it difficult to establish how much Nvidia stock Trump currently owns.Trump's investment accounts sold between $500,001 and $1 million worth of Nvidia shares on May 18, the first Monday after his return from a China visit with Huang. The sale was part of a wider trading spree, with Trump disclosing more than 21,000 trades in 2025, compared with roughly 500 during his entire first term, according to CNBC's analysis.The scale of Trump's Nvidia investments has also raised questions about his financial interests in the company, particularly given his close relationship with Huang and his administration's decisions on export controls.The administration has opened the door for Nvidia to do business in China, while Trump has repeatedly defended its approach to export restrictions against criticism. These decisions have come under scrutiny as the company faces questions over its China-related business and the allegations surrounding Huang.White House officials have repeatedly maintained that Trump does not personally select or trade individual stocks. The president has also rejected calls to sell his stock holdings.According to the White House, Trump's assets are held in a trust managed by his children, while independent financial managers handle his investment portfolio.Trump has also appeared to question his administration's assessment of Alice Huang's alleged links to Chinese intelligence.“I don’t know that she’s a spy at all. Nobody's proven that,” he told reporters outside the White House on Monday. “He probably shouldn’t have been doing, on a personal basis, what he did. You know, from — who knows? That's a different story. But nobody's proven that she's a spy. She may not be a spy,” he said.Nvidia shares were trading at around $157.72 on Monday, down more than 3.1% during the day. The decline came as investors reacted to Huang's resignation ahead of the company's third-quarter earnings call scheduled for Tuesday.Huang stepped down last Thursday following revelations about his relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer, who is suspected of being a spy.
Article Summary: Trump's investments in the AI chipmaker have grown sharply over the past year. Financial disclosures suggest that his stake could be worth as much as $62 million. Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have been actively buying and selling Nvidia shares.

Article Title: India faces 'acute' aircraft shortage, needs more than 1,000 planes: Piyush Goyal
Article Text:
Union minister Piyush Goyal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India is looking to add another 1,000 civilian aircraft to its existing orders as it struggles to keep up with rising air traffic demand amid an "acute" shortage of planes, Union minister Piyush Goyal said.The government is also pushing established aircraft manufacturers to speed up supplies.Speaking to reporters during his two-day visit to Egypt, Goyal said expanding the aircraft fleet would help improve air connectivity between the two countries and create room for more flights."We need to see more (air) connectivity... as we get more aircraft, we are sure we will be able to have more flights to Egypt," he said.Goyal is in Egypt to explore opportunities to strengthen trade and investment ties between the two countries. Currently, EgyptAir operates direct flights connecting India and Egypt.Pointing to the scale of India's aircraft requirements, the minister said the country had already ordered more than 1,200 planes but would need over 2,000 aircraft to meet its requirements. It is now prepared to place orders for another 1,000 planes, while pressing manufacturers to ensure quicker deliveries."We have ordered more than 1,200 planes, and we are ready to order another 1,000 planes; we need more than 2,000 planes for our requirements.So we are pursuing the established manufacturers of aircraft for faster supplies," Goyal said.He reiterated that the arrival of more aircraft would allow Indian airlines to operate additional flights to Egypt.India is one of the world's fastest-growing civil aviation markets, with airlines IndiGo and Air India having placed substantial aircraft orders with Airbus and Boeing for deliveries in the coming years.The country is also seeing the presence of several major international aerospace companies. Airbus has two final assembly lines in India, catering to military transport aircraft and helicopters.Global aircraft manufacturers Boeing and Airbus also source components and services worth around $2 billion every year from India. Meanwhile, Brazilian aircraft maker Embraer has partnered with the Adani Group under a strategic collaboration to explore setting up regional aircraft manufacturing in India.
Article Summary: India is looking to add another 1,000 civilian aircraft to its existing orders. The government is also pushing established aircraft manufacturers to speed up supplies. Union minister Piyush Goyal is in Egypt to explore opportunities to strengthen trade and investment ties between the two countries.

Article Title: IOC’s first SAF batch cleared for commercial supply
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has produced its first batch of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) through co-processing at Indian Oil Corporation (IOC)’s Panipat refinery, which has now been cleared for commercial supply, petroleum minister Hardeep Singh Puri said.The development marks a step towards meeting the country’s target of blending 1% SAF in jet fuel for international flights from Jan 1, 2027.In a post on X, Puri said used cooking oil was converted into aviation fuel at the refinery. He also announced that the first batch had received India’s first International Sustainability and Carbon Certification (ISCC) CORSIA certification for SAF production.Speaking at an industry event on Tuesday, IOC chairperson AS Sahney said the refinery had sufficient capacity to meet the initial blending requirement. The blending target will be raised to 2% in 2028 and 5% by 2030.India consumed over 9 million tonnes of aviation fuel in 2025-26, with demand projected to rise to 14 million tonnes by 2030.IOC had entered into an agreement with Air India in Aug last year for SAF supplies. Sahney said the company would firm up supply agreements with airlines before making investment decisions on additional SAF projects.IOC plans to produce around 35,000 tonnes of SAF annually at its Panipat facility, using used cooking oil collected from large hotel and restaurant chains.Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL), another state-run oil major, is setting up an SAF co-processing unit with an annual capacity of 61,000 tonnes at its Mumbai refinery. The unit is expected to begin production by Jan 2027. BPCL has also secured ISCC CORSIA certification for SAF production and signed an agreement with Akasa Air for its supply.SAF uses alternative raw materials such as used cooking oil and agricultural waste instead of conventional petroleum-based feedstocks. The fuel can be mixed with regular aviation turbine fuel, helping airlines lower emissions without requiring significant changes to aircraft or airport fuelling infrastructure.India’s SAF blending targets are in line with international efforts to reduce aviation-related emissions under the International Civil Aviation Organisation’s Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA).The civil aviation ministry has drawn up a draft National Sustainable Aviation Fuel Policy, proposing a national advisory council to coordinate efforts across ministries and oversee implementation. The draft also envisages public-private partnerships to encourage SAF production and the development of feedstock collection networks. It has been circulated to the petroleum ministry for comments.Civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu said building a domestic SAF ecosystem could help India save $5-7 billion annually on crude oil imports and raise farmers’ incomes by 10-15%.
Article Summary: India has produced its first batch of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) through co-processing at Indian Oil Corporation’s Panipat refinery. The development marks a step towards meeting the country's target of blending 1% SAF in jet fuel from Jan 1, 2027. The blending target will be raised to 2% in 2028 and 5% by 2030.

Article Title: No 24x7 trading in immediate future, Sebi chief flags cyber risks, liquidity concerns
Article Text:
No round the clock trading immediately

Equity tokenisation not feasible for now

Dual listing faces structural hurdles

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SEBI reviews key market regulations

NEW DELHI: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has no immediate plans to introduce round-the-clock stock market trading, with chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey flagging cybersecurity threats, fragmented liquidity and investor fatigue as key concerns. He said that extending market hours would require a strong justification, given the costs and operational risks involved.Speaking to the media on Wednesday on the sidelines of the 65th General Assembly and Annual Meeting of the World Federation of Exchanges (WFE), Pandey said tha the regulator needs to carefully weigh the potential risks before considering a shift to 24x7 trading."For the 24x7 approach, we should have a very strong kind of reason why should we do it, and what are the costs and what are the risks of that," Pandey told ANI. "Nobody has a clue of how they are going to handle the cybersecurity. Every day something is happening in the US."While he did not comment on extending existing trading hours, Pandey questioned whether longer sessions would necessarily improve market efficiency, pointing to their possible impact on liquidity and retail investors."People will complain that the prices have gone up at night while they were sleeping.Extending the market hours is not necessarily a very efficient way," he said.He also indicated that prediction markets were not a priority for the regulator.On distributed ledger technology (DLT), Pandey said corporate bond tokenisation was progressing through a three-phase pilot. However, extending the technology to equities was not viable at present because of the scale of India's equity market and the costs involved."Equity is a slightly different cup of tea," he said. "We have to see the efficiency of DLT technologies vis-a-vis equity market cap. DLT cannot handle it, and it will be a very costly technology."Pandey also highlighted two challenges to allowing Indian companies to list overseas: the absence of full rupee capital account convertibility and India's client-level segregation framework.India tracks individual investors through millions of accounts and around 1,000 clearing members. This differs from markets using omnibus accounts, where clearing corporations have limited visibility into individual end-clients. Aligning the two systems would involve technological challenges, he said."Dual listing would mean that your prices will simply equalize, and all kinds of investors should be capable of trading in all kinds of places," Pandey said.On other reforms, Pandey said Sebi was undertaking a comprehensive review of its Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR), and Innovators Growth Platform (IGP) norms, last overhauled in 2018.The regulator is also examining proposals concerning the Margin Trading Facility (MTF) and a pre-IPO platform.On Securities Lending and Borrowing (SLBM), Pandey said India would follow an exchange-traded model instead of opaque over-the-counter practices."We don't want anything dark pool or outside OTC kind of thing. We want it on exchanges," he said, emphasising the need for transparent market frameworks.
Article Summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has no immediate plans to introduce round-the-clock stock market trading. Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey flagged cybersecurity threats, fragmented liquidity and investor fatigue as key concerns. He said extending market hours would require a strong justification, given the costs and operational risks involved.

Article Title: OpenAI, Anthropic and other global AI firms expand in India as 24 overseas tech companies grow their combined workforce by over 30% to 24,000, with mid-career talent driving demand
Article Text:
Industry executives, including founders, staffing firms and analysts, attributed the trend to several factors.

Growing demand for India’s talent

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

There is a growing demand for India’s talent as global artificial intelligence (AI) and technology firms are turning to the country in greater numbers to recruit talent and develop products, with startups and mid-sized companies increasingly relying on the country’s engineers for product research and development.Despite India's large pool of engineers, competition for skilled professionals is intense, with domestic and international startups competing against IT services companies, global capability centres (GCCs) and businesses in other sectors, industry experts said.Kapil Joshi, CEO of IT staffing and IT solutions at Quess Corp, said professionals with four to 12 years of experience, capable of implementing AI solutions and taking projects into production, make up 55% of total demand.A group of 24 international AI and emerging technology companies, excluding Big Tech, tracked by staffing firm Xpheno, expanded their combined employee strength in India by over 30% in the past year to approximately 24,000.The companies span several segments, including AI, robotics, cybersecurity, fintech and enterprise software. The list includes Anthropic, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Perplexity, Replit, Wispr Flow, Databricks, Figma, Rippling, Harness and Glean.“India may not be comparable to Silicon Valley today in terms of the depth of its AI talent, but it has the potential,” Kamal Karanth, cofounder of Xpheno told ET.Pointing to the increasing number of emerging technology companies recruiting in India, he said, “From a future investment perspective, companies want to build that capability here.”The US has produced nearly 200 unicorns over the past two years, and many of these companies have access to talent in India, Karanth said.Industry executives, including founders, staffing firms and analysts, attributed the trend to several factors.These include the growing ability of Indian teams to build and customise technology products for global markets, as well as the challenges of recruiting talent in established technology centres such as San Francisco. These factors are prompting international technology companies to establish teams in India and expand their existing operations.Companies such as Rippling and Databricks are primarily interested in India’s engineering workforce, while ElevenLabs and Wispr Flow are expanding locally to serve their growing user base in the country, said Pratyush Choudhury, cofounder and general partner at AI-focused venture fund Activate.“For ElevenLabs and Wispr Flow, India became an important market early on…and they need local teams to adapt and customise their products for Indian users and customers ,” he said. India ranks as the second- or third-largest market outside the US for both companies, he added.Activate invests in early-stage startups working across AI applications, foundational models and infrastructure. Its portfolio includes both ElevenLabs and Wispr Flow.Choudhury, who also works closely with startups on recruitment, pointed to Wispr Flow’s Android product to illustrate how the Indian market has shaped product requirements. The need to address keyboard functionality and mobile usage became apparent as the company catered to Indian users.ElevenLabs, meanwhile, collaborated with Indian startups on developing models and sourcing data to train them.Manav Garg, former executive chairman of Emergent Labs, said the growing presence of founders and senior executives of Indian origin in Silicon Valley is also helping international startups establish operations in India. Garg is launching an agentic commerce startup backed by Flipkart and Navi cofounder Sachin Bansal.“The Indian diaspora in Silicon Valley has a better understanding of the local talent market and can leverage its connections to build teams here,” Garg said.
Article Summary: 24 international AI and emerging technology companies expanded their combined employee strength in India by over 30% in the past year. Industry executives, including founders, staffing firms and analysts, attributed the trend to several factors. Growing ability of Indian teams to build and customise technology products for global markets, as well as the challenges of recruiting talent in established technology centres.

Article Title: SpiceJet board approves Rs 5,500 crore fundraise plan to revive cash-strapped airline
Article Text:
File photo: SpiceJet flight on a tarmac

Fleet expansion plans amid financial pressure

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Cash-strapped budget airline SpiceJet has approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to strengthen its finances, rebuild its fleet and support its revival.The airline's board cleared the fundraising plan at a meeting on Wednesday, after being briefed on investment discussions with potential new investors. The proposed capital raise will be carried out through a combination of equity and other permitted instruments, subject to the necessary shareholder and regulatory approvals, SpiceJet said in a statement.The board has also approved a proposal to increase the company's authorised share capital from Rs 2,000 crore to Rs 7,500 crore, subject to the required approvals. It has directed the management to expedite the fundraising process.The move comes as SpiceJet faces mounting pressure on its operations and finances. Its domestic market share fell to 0.6% in September from 1.2% in August, according to the latest data from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA).The airline attributed the strain to geopolitical disruptions and airspace restrictions, alongside a sharp rise in aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices, which it said had more than doubled over the past few months.The proposed fundraise is expected to provide funds to strengthen its balance sheet, support fleet expansion and meet operational requirements.SpiceJet has been working to expand its operational fleet even as it struggles with aircraft groundings, payment pressures and a cash crunch. The airline had announced in September that it had finalised lease agreements with three aircraft operators to induct 20 planes ahead of the winter schedule.The planned additions comprise 15 Boeing and five Airbus aircraft under damp and wet lease arrangements, with phased induction scheduled between mid-October and mid-November.The airline had earlier outlined plans to increase operations to around 200 daily flights during the winter schedule, with higher frequencies on key routes and expanded domestic and international connectivity. It currently operates around nine aircraft from its own fleet, alongside a number of wet-leased planes.SpiceJet had also received Rs 150 crore under the Centre's Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS), the government said in September, adding that the aviation regulator was monitoring the airline's operations and financial position.The carrier is also facing legal and payment-related challenges, including insolvency petitions filed by lessors and claims involving former promoter Kalanithi Maran and KAL Airways.SpiceJet chairman and managing director Ajay Singh said the proposed fundraising would provide an opportunity to rebuild the airline, strengthen operations and restore the brand.Shares of SpiceJet rose nearly 5% to Rs 9.97 apiece in late afternoon trade on the BSE on Wednesday.
Article Summary: SpiceJet has approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to strengthen its finances, rebuild its fleet and support its revival. The airline's board cleared the fundraising plan at a meeting on Wednesday. The proposed capital raise will be carried out through a combination of equity and other permitted instruments, subject to the necessary shareholder and regulatory approvals.

Article Title: Chinese steel imports threaten Indian industry, Tata Steel CEO calls for level playing field
Article Text:
Representative image

Tata Steel targets 40 million tonnes of capacity

Rising costs and overseas coal sourcing

Tata Steel discusses carbon duties and European assistance

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Chinese steel imports remain a threat to India's domestic steel industry, Tata Steel MD and CEO T V Narendran said on Wednesday, stressing that Indian manufacturers investing heavily in expanding capacity should not be unfairly affected by the influx of cheaper imports."We should make sure that Indian industry which is investing significant capital in building capacity, should not be unfairly impacted," Narendran told reporters on the sidelines of an event in New Delhi.He said steel producers were continuing discussions with the government on measures to protect the domestic industry. His remarks come amid concerns over rising Chinese steel exports, which Narendran said currently exceed 10 million tonnes a month and could reach 130 million tonnes in 2026.Reuters reported in October that India's steel ministry was unlikely to seek fresh curbs on cheap imports in the near term, despite calls from domestic producers for stronger protection.China accounted for nearly a third of India's finished steel imports in the first half of the current financial year.Narendran said Tata Steel had the potential to increase its annual production capacity to 40 million tonnes between 2033 and 2035, with scope to eventually go beyond that level.He indicated that existing capacities could offer room to reach 50 million tonnes, although investments would be guided by business requirements."I'm quite confident that the construction to achieve 40 million tonnes will be well underway across our sites," he said, while indicating that reaching the target by 2030 may not be possible.The company plans to finalise the third phase of its Kalinganagar expansion next year, taking the plant's capacity to 13 million tonnes. The capacity of Bhushan Steel is also expected to rise to 6.5 million tonnes, while the expansion of Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited (NINL) has already been announced.Tata Steel is also considering one or two additional electric arc furnace projects. Narendran said the company would weigh investments in areas such as downstream operations alongside rising raw material costs.Narendran said iron ore costs were increasing in India, while Tata Steel would continue importing 60-70 per cent of its coking coal requirements because imported coal has lower ash content.The company sources most of its imported coking coal from Australia, with smaller volumes coming from Indonesia. Narendran said Tata Steel preferred to remain a buyer rather than invest in overseas coal mines, with its supply arrangements largely supported by partnerships with Australian suppliers.He said the company had no plans to invest in overseas coking coal mines.On the European Union's carbon duties on steel imports, Narendran said the debate reflected the differing interests of Indian and European producers, with both sides seeking a level playing field based on their manufacturing costs.European steelmakers want imported steel to face the same carbon tax as locally manufactured products, while Indian producers oppose paying an additional tax to access the European market, he said."As a producer of steel in the EU, there is a carbon tax that we pay in the EU, so obviously the steel industry in the EU will say that if I'm paying a carbon tax, anyone who sells in Europe should pay the same carbon tax," Narendran said."If I'm sitting in India, I will say why should I pay a carbon tax if I have to sell in the EU," he added.His remarks come after the European Commission imposed a 9.5 per cent anti-dumping duty on certain cold-rolled flat steel products from India, including those manufactured by Tata Steel and JSW Steel.The duties took effect on November 17 and form part of a wider measure covering five countries, with rates reaching up to 27.9 per cent, according to Reuters.The investigation followed a complaint filed by European steel association Eurofer in 2025. The European Commission cited government measures that it said had distorted domestic iron ore prices in India.Separately, Narendran said Tata Steel had sought financial assistance from the Dutch government for a project, with discussions still underway. He noted that the general benchmark in Europe was for governments to support at least 40 per cent of a project's capital expenditure.
Article Summary: Chinese steel imports remain a threat to India's domestic steel industry, Tata Steel CEO says. Article Title: Anthropic IPO: How to buy shares, expected price and risks investors should know

AI giant Anthropic is preparing for its stock market debut, giving individual investors an opportunity to own a stake in the company behind chatbot Claude. The initial public offering (IPO) is expected to value the company at $1.4 trillion (£1 trillion), making it one of the biggest stock market listings in history.Investor demand is already strong, with reports suggesting that the offering is nearly six times oversubscribed. However, the IPO comes amid volatility in US markets, particularly technology stocks.Here is what investors need to know about the share price, application process and risks before deciding whether to invest.According to the company's prospectus, Anthropic is offering 825 million shares of Class A common stock at an initial price range of $70 to $78 per share. The final price will be decided on Wednesday.The shares will carry voting rights, but all the votes combined will account for only 49.9% of the total voting power. This means investors will not have enough voting rights to force changes in how the company is run.The shares are scheduled to list on the Nasdaq in New York on Thursday. Both individual investors and large institutions will be able to participate.Investors in the UK can subscribe to Anthropic shares through AJ Bell, Hargreaves Lansdown, Robinhood and eToro.The minimum investment differs across platforms.Robinhood and eToro require a minimum investment of $250 (£189), while Hargreaves Lansdown has set the minimum at £250. AJ Bell requires at least £1,000.The application deadlines are 1pm on Wednesday for AJ Bell and 3pm for Hargreaves Lansdown and Robinhood. All three platforms have warned that applications could close earlier without notice.Those who miss the IPO can still buy shares once they begin trading on the Nasdaq. They will also be available through platforms that are not participating in the offering.Direct investment is not the only way to gain exposure to Anthropic. Some funds already hold stakes in the company.In the UK, these include the Baillie Gifford US Growth and Scottish Mortgage investment trusts. Fidelity also has investments in funds available to US investors.After the listing, Anthropic shares are expected to enter some tracker funds, although the timing will vary. Actively managed funds may also choose to buy the stock. This means investors could gain exposure through their existing fund investments without purchasing shares directly.Strong demand does not necessarily mean the shares will deliver lasting returns. Anthropic's prospectus includes 92 pages detailing potential risks to the company and its industry. Recent volatility in US markets, particularly technology stocks, is another factor investors need to consider.The company's governance structure has also attracted scrutiny. The Guardian's financial editor Nils Pratley has raised concerns, saying it “represents an extraordinary concentration of power in the hands of a few individuals”.Jason Hollands, managing director of investment platform Bestinvest by Evelyn Partners, which is not participating in the IPO, has also highlighted concerns about the company's profitability.“Anthropic would give most retail investors the first opportunity to have a direct stake in a frontier AI developer. But it remains a capital-intensive business, and it has yet to establish a consistent path to profitability,” he told The Guardian. “Investors will need to judge whether the company can turn demand for its models into durable earnings.”Hollands says strong demand and limited share supply could push up the stock initially, but that does not guarantee sustained gains.
Article Summary: Anthropic is offering 825 million shares of Class A common stock at an initial price range of $70 to $78 per share. The shares are scheduled to list on the Nasdaq in New York on Thursday. Both individual investors and large institutions will be able to participate.

Article Title: Bombay HC quashes ICICI Bank’s sanction to prosecute ex-CEO Chanda Kochhar
Article Text:
The Bombay High Court annulled ICICI Bank's sanction to prosecute Chanda Kochhar, citing incomplete assessment in the decision-making process.

Bombay High Court on Wednesday set aside ICICI Bank ’s sanction to prosecute its former CEO Chanda Kochhar in connection with alleged irregularities in loans extended to the videocon group, led by Venugopal Dhoot.According to news agency PTI, a single-judge bench of justice Milind Jadhav ruled that the authority granting the sanction had failed to apply its mind to the material placed before it.“The impugned sanction dated May 15, 2023, is illegal and deserves to be quashed on the ground that the authority that granted the same is not a competent authority and it completely failed to apply its mind to the material, or lack thereof, placed before it while granting sanction,” the court observed.The High Court said the sanction order was legally unsustainable and therefore null and void.The court delivered its verdict on a petition filed by Kochhar, who argued that ICICI Bank had not followed the prescribed procedure while approving the sanction for her prosecution.The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested Kochhar and her husband, Deepak Kochhar, in December 2022 in connection with the alleged loan fraud.The couple received interim bail in January 2023.In June 2023, the CBI told a special court in Mumbai that ICICI Bank had approved the sanction to prosecute Kochhar because there appeared to be a quid pro quo, an exchange of favours in the loan extended to videocon.Such approval is mandatory under the prevention of corruption act because bank employees are treated as public servants under the law.The case relates to a Rs 3,250-crore loan that ICICI Bank sanctioned to the videocon group in 2012, when Kochhar was at the helm of the bank. The CBI has alleged cheating and irregularities in the loan approval process.According to the investigating agency, Kochhar cleared the loan because her husband and family members stood to benefit from the transaction. In return, videocon allegedly invested in Nu renewable, a company linked to her husband, the CBI has claimed.The loan later turned into a non-performing asset (NPA) and was classified as a bank fraud case.
Article Summary: Bombay High Court set aside ICICI Bank’s sanction to prosecute its former CEO Chanda Kochhar. The case relates to alleged irregularities in loans extended to the videocon group, led by Venugopal Dhoot. CBI has alleged cheating and irregularities in the loan approval process.

Article Title: ePlane picks US firm Lynx's software platform for e200X electric aircraft
Article Text:

BENGALURU: India’s The ePlane Company has selected US-based Lynx Software Technologies’ “LYNX MOSA.ic platform” to run multiple software systems on its e200X electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, enabling safety-critical and mission-specific applications to operate on shared computing modules without interfering with each other.Announced at the eVTOL Show USA on Nov 18, the partnership will see the software platform used for mission computing aboard the e200X, a three-seat aircraft (one pilot and two passengers) being developed for air ambulance, urban cargo and passenger services.The aircraft has a modular airframe, with different configurations carrying varying payloads, sensor systems and software requirements. However, flight control systems need to remain deterministic and certifiable across all configurations.LYNX MOSA.ic addresses this through a partitioned computing architecture. Flight-critical applications, including vehicle and energy management systems, will operate in dedicated ARINC 653 partitions, isolated from lower-criticality functions such as sensor data processing and enhanced situational awareness.Heavy artificial intelligence processing will run on a separate platform, with the mission system providing controlled interfaces between it and the rest of the aircraft.This separation is intended to maintain safety and cybersecurity boundaries while allowing mission-specific software to evolve.The platform is built around a separation kernel-based Type 1 hypervisor, which assigns individual software applications dedicated space and time partitions. It is certifiable to DO-178C Design Assurance Level A, a standard for safety-critical airborne software.Prof Satya Chakravarthy, founder and technical lead of The ePlane Company, said the technology would allow the company to isolate safety-critical systems while developing additional aircraft functionalities.Founded in 2019 and incubated at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras, ePlane is developing the e200X as a multi-role electric aircraft. Its flagship vehicle is the first eVTOL aircraft accepted into the Directorate General of Civil Aviation's official type-certification pipeline, according to the company.

It envisages collaboration in research translation, technology transfers, entrepreneurship and access to funding opportunities in India and France,” C-CAMP said.The partnership will focus on areas including synthetic biology, genomics and biotechnology. It also proposes a pilot startup exchange programme that will offer entrepreneurs from both ecosystems opportunities for immersion, mentoring, access to curated investor networks and state-of-the-art research facilities.The two organisations will also explore exchanges of startup and technology portfolios to facilitate international incubation, establish launchpads for market entry and support the commercialisation of technologies.“The agreement provides for exploring joint funding opportunities through existing Indo-French govt collaborations, including the CEFIPRA/IFCPAR programme, as well as upcoming European Union programmes such as Horizon Europe,” C-CAMP said.C-CAMP director and CEO Taslimarif Saiyed said the partnership would seek to advance both deep science and impact-driven science translation, enabling technologies with applications in India and France. He said this was the organisation's second collaboration with the French innovation ecosystem, following an earlier partnership with Paris Santé.Genopole director-general David Bodet said both ecosystems faced challenges relating to high manufacturing costs and the ability to scale production to industrial levels. Combining expertise, he said, could help researchers and entrepreneurs address these constraints.The collaboration will seek to support the development of new therapies and technologies while also exploring biotechnology applications in industrial decarbonisation and environmental transition.

Article Title: Nepal to buy up to 350 MW power from India as hydropower output falls
Article Text:
Nepal has been granted clearance to import up to 350 MW of electricity from India, a crucial step for winter preparedness. (Pic Credit: Agency)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India has granted Nepal permission to import up to 350 MW of electricity during the winter season to meet its domestic demand. The approval comes as the country’s hydropower generation declined and several power projects remain damaged by recent floods.The central electricity authority (CEA), under India's ministry of power, has authorised the Nepal electricity authority (NEA), the state-owned power utility, to purchase electricity from the Indian energy exchange (IEX) at competitive rates for up to 17 hours daily, NEA officials said.NEA managing direction Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha said that the approval will remain valid from November 17, 2026, to July 31, 2027. The move is expected to help Nepal bridge the seasonal gap between electricity demand and domestic production, according to news agency PTI.Under the approved arrangement, Nepal can import 300 MW through the Kataiya-Kushaha, Ramnagar-Surajpura and Raxaul-Parwanipur transmission lines. An additional 50 MW can be sourced through the new nautanwa-mainahiya transmission line.Nepal's heavy reliance on run-of-the-river hydropower projects makes its electricity production dependent on seasonal changes in river flows.During summer, increased water levels allow the country to generate surplus electricity, much of which is exported to India. However, falling river levels during winter reduce hydropower output, compelling Nepal to depend on electricity imports to meet domestic requirements.The country's power generation capacity has also been affected by damage to several hydropower projects in central Nepal during the devastating Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi floods in August.Power projects with a combined installed capacity of 431 MW have remained disconnected from the national grid since the disaster, further straining domestic electricity supplies.However, officials expect domestic generation to recover from mid-April as river water levels begin to rise. The improvement could reduce Nepal's reliance on imported electricity and potentially enable the country to resume power exports.
Article Summary: Nepal has been granted permission to import up to 350 MW of electricity from India. The approval comes as the country’s hydropower generation declined and several power projects remain damaged by recent floods. The move is expected to help Nepal bridge the seasonal gap between electricity demand and domestic production.

The US dollar remained close to a 19-month high on Wednesday as steady retail sales, rising import prices and comments from Federal Reserve officials strengthened expectations of another interest rate hike in December.The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, edged up 0.05% to 103.66 after touching 103.78 overnight, its highest level since April 2, 2025.The euro slipped 0.12% to $1.0984, while the Japanese yen weakened 0.06% to 159.46 per dollar. Sterling also lost 0.06% to trade at $1.32.US retail sales rose 0.2% in October, matching market expectations, while import prices increased 1.1%, against forecasts of a 0.7% rise. The figures reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates by 25 basis points next month. Traders are pricing in such a move, according to the CME FedWatch tool."Overall, the report reinforces our view that further interest rate hikes from the Fed are warranted in order to counter demand-pull inflation," Henry Russell, a London-based economist for ANZ, said about the US sales data. "The strength of domestic demand in the US, in our view, warrants a decisive monetary policy response from the Fed."Investors are awaiting US housing starts data for October, due later on Wednesday. Analysts expect the figure to increase to 1.245 million from 1.221 million in September, while building permits are projected to decline.Federal Reserve officials' comments will also be in focus. New York Fed President John Williams, who said on Tuesday that further rate increases would likely be needed to tackle high inflation, is expected to speak again. Fed Board Governor Michael Barr and Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari are also scheduled to address separate events. The central bank's meeting minutes from last month, when it kept rates unchanged, are due on Thursday.Meanwhile, the yen weakened despite Japan reporting a 20.5% year-on-year increase in exports in October, beating the 20% market forecast. Exports rose for the 14th consecutive month, reaching a record monthly value on strong semiconductor demand.The growth followed a 16.5% increase in September.The Australian dollar was little changed at $0.673 after touching its weakest level since January 19, while the New Zealand dollar gained 0.05% to $0.5495, recovering slightly from a 19-month low recorded on Tuesday.Broader market sentiment remained cautious following a selloff in AI and technology stocks, driven by Nvidia CEO's sudden departure, a Democratic sweep in US midterm elections and concerns over debt-funded AI infrastructure expansion.
Article Summary: The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, edged up 0.05% to 103.66. The euro slipped 0.12% to $1.0984, while the Japanese yen weakened 0.06% to 159.46 per dollar. US retail sales rose 0.2% in October, matching market expectations.

Article Title: Oil prices today: Crude falls as US inventories rise; Iran tensions limit losses
Article Text:
Representative image

US-Iran conflict keeps supply concerns alive

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Houthi drone claims add to regional risks

Oil prices declined on Wednesday after industry data showed a sharp increase in US crude and fuel inventories last week, although continued hostilities between the United States and Iran and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz limited the fall.US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures dropped 56 cents, or 0.65%, to $85.45 a barrel, while Brent crude futures fell 16 cents, or 0.17%, to $92.98 a barrel as of 1.49 am GMT, according to Reuters.Market sources said US crude stocks increased by 5.28 million barrels in the week ended November 13, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) released on Tuesday.Gasoline inventories rose by 5.12 million barrels, while distillate stocks increased by 351,000 barrels.The inventory build put pressure on prices, but concerns over supply disruptions in the Middle East continued to support the market.Oil benchmarks had settled higher on Tuesday as the conflict between Washington and Tehran intensified, despite continuing talks involving Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar.Bahrain's defence force said on Wednesday it had intercepted Iranian aerial attacks on the country, which hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet.The development followed an exchange of strikes between the US and Iran a day earlier.Iranian drones attacked a US military radar system in Bahrain on Tuesday, prompting Washington to strike a missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island, Reuters reported.Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has also faced continued risks. An LPG tanker was hit by a projectile while sailing through the waterway off Oman's coast on Monday, forcing its crew to evacuate.The strait is a key route for global energy shipments, and attacks on vessels have added to concerns over the movement of oil and other fuel supplies.“Although regional supply may continue to recover through alternative routes, the latest vessel data suggests that normalization of flows through Hormuz is still not possible under current conditions,” LSEG analysts said in a note on Tuesday.Supply concerns have also extended beyond the immediate US-Iran confrontation. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group said on Tuesday that it had launched five drones towards two pumping stations along Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline.Saudi Arabia has been using the pipeline during the conflict to reroute oil to its Yanbu port for export, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.The latest developments have kept attention on the security of alternative export routes as the conflict continues, even as rising US crude and fuel inventories weigh on prices.
Article Summary: US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures dropped 56 cents, or 0.65%, to $85.45 a barrel. Brent crude futures fell 16 cents,or 0.17, to $92.98 a barrel as of 1.49 am GMT. Market sources said US crude stocks increased by 5.28 million barrels in the week ended November 13.

Article Title: 'Board accepted his resignation': Nvidia chairman rules out Jensen Huang's return; company doubles revenue
Article Text:
Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (File photo)

Also Read |

Nvidia earnings double; report makes no mention of Huang

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(With AP inputs)

Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones on Tuesday ruled out Jensen Huang's return, saying the board does not intend to reinstate him as CEO.The company's revenue, meanwhile, soared more than 100% year-on-year."The board of directors unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Jones said at the start of Nvidia's quarterly earnings call.His statement came hours after Huang expressed his desire to return to the company if invited.Huang, who left Nvidia last week following revelations of an extramarital affair and other alleged relationships, made his first public comments since his departure in a social media post. Acknowledging "serious mistakes" in his personal life, he said he would be "honoured" to return if the board believed it was in the best interests of the company, its shareholders, employees and the country.His possible return had drawn support from several technology industry figures, including Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. US President Donald Trump has also backed his reinstatement, saying the Taiwan-born executive had "learned a big lesson".An online petition urging Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang has attracted support from current and former employees, investors and other Silicon Valley figures. Its organisers questioned whether his departure had followed due process and called for an independent investigation into the allegations.Meanwhile, Nvidia made no mention of Huang's departure or possible return in its third-quarter earnings statement released on Tuesday.The chipmaker reported revenue of more than $116 billion, double the figure from a year earlier and above Wall Street estimates. Net income stood at $2.70 per share, beating analysts' expectations of $2.48.Chief financial officer Colette Kress was expected to address Wall Street analysts on the earnings call for the first time since being named interim CEO following Huang's departure.His exit followed revelation of a relationships with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected of having links to Beijing's intelligence services and a senior Nvidia executive who reported to him.The businesswoman was an executive at Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International, which is under US investigation for allegedly violating export controls by diverting advanced Nvidia AI chips to Chinese companies.
Article Summary: Chairman Harvey Jones says the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. His statement came hours after Huang expressed his desire to return to the company if invited. Huang left Nvidia last week following revelations of an extramarital affair and other alleged relationships.

Article Title: Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney dies at 95; started global chain with $600 loan from mother
Article Text:
Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney.

Who was Dan Carney?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Wichita State pays tribute

Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney, who turned a $600 loan from his mother into one of the world's biggest pizza chains alongside his brother Frank, has died at the age of 95.Carney died peacefully on November 13, surrounded by his family, according to an obituary published by his family. No cause of death was disclosed. The New York Post reported his death on Monday, citing the obituary.Carney and his brother Frank founded Pizza Hut in 1958 in Wichita, Kansas, when Dan was 26. The brothers borrowed $600 from their mother to set up their first restaurant, which opened near Wichita State University.The venture took off despite pizza being relatively unfamiliar to many American diners at the time. Within a year, the brothers began franchising the business, which subsequently expanded into an international restaurant chain.In 1977, PepsiCo acquired Pizza Hut for $300 million. Frank, who had served as the company's CEO, left the position in 1980. He died in December 2020 at the age of 82 after battling pneumonia.Born in Kansas City, Missouri, Carney grew up in a large family and was one of 12 siblings, according to the NYP. He graduated from Wichita State University in 1953 with a bachelor's degree in business administration.He subsequently served two years in the US Air Force as a first lieutenant before returning to his academic pursuits.He received his master's degree in 2004, 51 years after completing his undergraduate studies.Carney married his childhood sweetheart, Beverly Singleton, in February 1954. The couple had six children and 12 grandchildren. Beverly died in 1998. Carney later married Gayla Coulter in 2001, and she survives him.Beyond his business career, Carney was involved in philanthropy and served as chairman of the board of the Cerebral Palsy Research Foundation of Kansas for 50 years.His obituary described him as a leader known for his integrity, generosity and commitment to mentoring others.“Dan was revolutionary in the franchise world,” the obituary said, adding that he was an investor not just in businesses but also in people.Wichita State University, Carney's alma mater, also paid tribute to the entrepreneur, recalling his contribution to the institution and the wider community.In a Facebook post on Monday, the university described him as an entrepreneur, philanthropist and proud Shocker whose impact would be felt for generations.The university also highlighted his humility, wisdom and belief in giving back, saying his mentorship had shaped the lives of students and colleagues.The original Pizza Hut building, where the brothers launched their business, has been preserved on the Wichita State campus. It now houses the Pizza Hut Museum, which opened to the public in 2018.Carney had attended the museum's opening and described seeing the original building as a humbling experience, according to a Wichita State University press release.
Article Summary: Carney and his brother Frank founded Pizza Hut in 1958 in Wichita, Kansas, when Dan was 26. The brothers borrowed $600 from their mother to set up their first restaurant, which opened near Wichita State University. Within a year, the brothers began franchising the business, which subsequently expanded into an international restaurant chain.

Article Title: US reveals how Megaspeed came under scrutiny and landed on Nvidia's 'no sell' list in 2025
Article Text:
Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore sales after cutting off Megaspeed

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia's partnership with Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed hit a roadblock in June 2025, when the chipmaker put it on its "no sell" list. The decision came after US investigators sought details of Nvidia's direct and indirect sales to its Asia-Pacific partner, according to information released by the US commerce and justice departments on Monday.The US investigation, however, had started much earlier, in 2024, after authorities flagged suspicious activity linked to the possible diversion of sensitive semiconductors.The commerce department approached Nvidia in May 2025, seeking records of direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed. A month later, the company found itself on Nvidia's restricted sales list, the two departments said in a joint statement.The agencies said the probe was triggered by suspicious activity detected through monitoring of potential semiconductor diversion."After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductor diversion, the department of commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations," the agencies said, as cited by Reuters.The investigation moved beyond records and sales checks in June 2025, when US agents travelled to Megaspeed's premises with Singaporean law enforcement officials. They carried out an "on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed" and questioned Alice Huang, who was then the company's chief executive.The Justice Department subsequently took charge of the criminal investigation into Megaspeed, following the enforcement action.The two departments said they were making details of the case public despite the usual practice of not commenting on ongoing investigations, citing public interest.Megaspeed's dealings with Nvidia are not the only aspect of the company drawing suspicion. Its former executive Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman, has also come under scrutiny, with some US authorities suspecting links to Chinese espionage efforts. However, Beijing has continued to refute the allegations.The allegations gained attention following reports that Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Huang. Jensen resigned from Nvidia on November 12. en unable to reach Alice Huang for comment.Megaspeed said on Sunday that Alice Huang formally left the company on August 30, 2025. It also maintained that it had conducted a "legitimate and lawful business."Singapore's government had said last week that Alice Huang previously held three key positions at Megaspeed — chief executive, chairperson and one of its key controllers.Police found insufficient evidence to establish that she had committed offences related to suspected false declarations over server purchases. However, they warned her for knowingly providing inaccurate information that played down her role in the company.Singapore has barred Alice Huang from re-entering the country. Investigations involving Megaspeed and six other individuals are still underway, the home affairs ministry said.Meanwhile, Singapore's government said on Monday that it had agreed to continue discussions with Washington over the company.
Article Summary: N Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore sales after cutting off Megaspeed in June 2025. US investigators sought details of Nvidia's direct and indirect sales to its Asia-Pacific partner. US investigation started much earlier, in 2024, after authorities flagged suspicious activity linked to possible diversion of sensitive semiconductors.

Article Title: Oil prices fall as rising supply outweighs Middle East tensions and fears of tanker attacks
Article Text:
Oil eases as Middle East supply worry subsides

Oil prices plunged marginally on Tuesday, with the prospect of a global supply surplus taking precedence over concerns about attacks on oil tankers in the Middle East. The possibility of rising supplies has weighed on the market even as tensions continue to threaten energy infrastructure and shipping routes in the region.WTI crude was down 48 cents, or 0.56%, at $85.24, while Brent crude declined 57 cents, or 0.62%, to $91.87. Prices were quoted with a 10-minute delay.Earlier on Friday, the International Energy Agency said that global oil market would move back into surplus in the fourth quarter of this year. The agency attributed this outlook to Middle East exports recovering at a faster pace than global oil demand, despite attacks on shipping.However, the security situation in the region remains a concern. Attacks on energy infrastructure and vessels in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz have continued, keeping uncertainty around a major global oil-export route.Though, geopolitical concerns are still present, they no longer having as much influence on prices as the supply outlook.Meanwhile, OPEC held a virtual meeting on Monday to discuss its assessment of members' maximum sustainable production capacity.The review is an important exercise as it will help establish OPEC+ production quotas for 2027 and subsequent years.The broader OPEC+ alliance, which also includes oil-producing countries led by Russia, is set to meet on November 29. The meeting will focus on deciding the group's oil output policy for 2027.In another development, US crude inventories held in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve declined to 276.4 million barrels last week, marking their lowest level since August 1982, according to Department of Energy data.The latest reduction is part of an agreement by the US to release 172 million barrels of oil from the reserve.
